settings._push_budget_note: LINE bills (requests x recipients), NOT message objects: one request carries up to 5 text objects of ~4,900 chars for the price of one. Arithmetic: line_monthly_quota/line_recipients = 300/2 = 150 requests per month; summary_reserve_per_day (3 digests) x 31 days = 93 reserved, leaving ~57 requests/month for realtime alerts (~2/day = alert_push_budget_per_day). A whole cycle of alerts is packed into ONE request, so this budget is per CYCLE, not per news item. When the daily budget is spent, only alert_override_levels items may still fire, at most alert_override_max_per_day extra requests; everything else waits for the next cycle or the daily digest (nothing is dropped). quota_warn_ratio: append a quota warning to the digest once the month passes this fraction of the plan.
settings._lookback_note: Freshness window: an article whose actual publication time is older than this many hours is ignored (never stored/alerted), regardless of dedup state. Comparison is timezone-aware in Asia/Bangkok.
settings._drop_if_no_date_note: When an item has NO parseable published date (e.g. gov listing links): false = keep it (conservative, preserves gov signal), true = drop it (strict).

settings._priority_alert_note: Critical keywords so central to this company's survival (TIS standards on rebar / IF furnaces, and anti-dumping measures) that a YELLOW item mentioning one still fires an instant alert instead of waiting for the daily digest. Everything else still needs RED/ORANGE. Rationale: the 2026-08-26 headline 'ขยับ 4 มอก. เป็นสินค้าควบคุม' scored exactly 4 (YELLOW) and would have been silently digested.
